sections.title: Reading Comprehension · Passage B
sections.intro: Read “To a Snake” and answer questions 10–14.

passage.title: To a Snake
passage.credit: —Jeffrey Harrison · “To a Snake” · from Into Daylight (2014), Tupelo Press

lines.text: I knew you were not poisonous
when I saw you in the side garden;
even your name—milk snake—
sounds harmless, and yet your pattern
of copper splotches outlined in black
frightened me, and the way you were
curled in loops; and it offended me
that you were so close to the house
and clearly living underneath it
if not inside, in the cellar, where I
have found your torn shed skins.
You must have been frightened too
when I caught you in the webbing
of the lacrosse stick and flung you
into the woods, where you landed
dangling from a vine-covered branch,
shamelessly twisted. Now I
am the one who is ashamed, unable
to untangle my feelings,
braided into my DNA or buried
deep in the part of my brain
that is most like yours.

questions.prompt: The speaker’s reaction to the snake (lines 1 through 6) was triggered by
questions.explanation: Although the speaker knows the milk snake is not poisonous, its copper splotches outlined in black frighten the speaker. Its coloring, not an aggressive act, triggers that initial reaction.

questions.prompt: The word “if” in line 10 indicates the speaker

choices.text: provokes a response from the snake
tolerates that the snake lives near the garden
respects the needs of the snake
resents that the snake goes into the cellar

questions.explanation: The speaker is offended that the snake lives under the house and suspects it may even enter the cellar, where shed skins have been found. “If not inside” conveys this unwelcome possibility.

questions.prompt: The use of “the lacrosse stick” (line 14) to move the snake most likely suggests
questions.explanation: The speaker catches the snake in the stick's webbing and immediately flings it into the woods. That improvised, forceful action suggests a hurried response to fear rather than careful or gentle handling.

questions.prompt: The phrase “shamelessly twisted” (line 17) emphasizes the speaker’s
questions.explanation: The speaker calls the flung snake “shamelessly twisted,” then immediately says “Now I am the one who is ashamed.” That contrast reveals guilt about having thrown the animal into the woods.

questions.prompt: Lines 17 through 22 demonstrate a shift in mood from
questions.explanation: The speaker initially hesitates over mixed feelings about the harmless but frightening snake. After flinging it away, the speaker explicitly feels ashamed and cannot untangle those feelings, so regret replaces the earlier uncertainty.
